BC001 indicates a function the bytecode compiler tagged evaluator-only
(EvalOnly) is reachable under --strict-bytecode, where no evaluator
bridge is wired. Reported by `ailang check --strict-bytecode` and by a
strict run or test before dispatch, instead of a mid-run VM CALL trap
(M-BYTECODE-STRICT-256-REG-CEILING Phase A).

records.summary: --verify-contracts is not enforced on the bytecode VM
records.fix_hint:
CTR004 refuses `run --verify-contracts` together with `--bytecode` or
`--strict-bytecode` (including under --batch): the VM does not enforce
contracts yet, so the combination used to run unchecked and exit 0
(#1956, M-RUNTIME-CONTRACT-PARITY M1). Lifted when the VM enforces them.

records.summary: extern func is not supported (the Go emitter that implemented it was removed)
records.fix_hint:
EXT004 indicates an `extern func` declaration. Extern functions were
implemented only in Go emitted by `ailang compile --emit-go`, which was
removed (#2389); no engine can run one, so the declaration itself is an
error, called or not (#2390). EXT001-EXT003 were the parser's shape
checks for the same declaration and are retired with it.

MOD007 indicates a duplicate module-scope binding: a module-level let/letrec
and a func (or two lets) declared with the same name. Silent shadowing was a
soundness trap once module lets and funcs share one declaration space
(M-MODULE-LET-FUNC-RESOLUTION, #366) — now a loud compile error.
MOD010 indicates module/path mismatch (e.g., module foo/bar but file is foo/baz.ail)

MOD011 indicates a cross-FILE module-name collision (two files declaring the
same module path), detected in the module pipeline. NOTE: per-file duplicate
module declarations are a PARSE-time diagnostic (MOD002 /
PAR_MODULE_PLACEMENT), not MOD011 — the old "multiple module declarations per
file" comment here was stale (M-PROMPT-FOOTGUNS).

records.summary: Shared module_prefix between root and dependency
records.fix_hint:
MOD013 indicates two packages share the same module_prefix, causing
ambiguous import resolution when one of them is the root project

records.summary: Imported name collides with a module-level definition or another import
records.fix_hint:
MOD015 indicates an ambiguous module-scope name: a selectively imported name
(import M (x) or import M (y as x)) that a module-level func, let or
constructor also defines, or that two imports bind to different exports.
The import used to win silently; now a compile error naming both sites
(#1467). MOD014 is the module-less-file error raised inline by the pipeline.

records.summary: Re-export cycle (export import chain returns to itself)
records.fix_hint:
MOD016 indicates a re-export cycle: `export import` lines whose chain of
re-exported names returns to a name already on it (M-PKG-PARALLEL-AGENTS C1).
